text:
Anna: Heads-up — nightly microloop CI flagged a latency regression on Ampere for candidate kernel 'KX-17' at seq=2048. p50 +12%, p99 +18% vs baseline.

perf-bot: [CI] nightly-microloop | arch=ampere seq=2048 kernel=KX-17 delta_p50=+12.1% delta_p99=+17.9% | https://ci.redwood/pipelines/7732/results

Ben: Do we have the raw microbench command/log to repro?

Anna: Ran a local repro, command: `./kbench --arch=ampere --kernel=KX-17 --seq=2048 --batch=4 --runs=200`

Anna: sample output snippet:
```
p50: 3.45ms -> 3.87ms (+12.1%)
p90: 4.90ms -> 5.40ms (+10.2%)
p99: 7.8ms -> 9.2ms (+17.9%)
kvcache_hits: 118234
kvcache_misses: 12345
avg_kv_size: 512 bytes
CPU-util: 28%  GPU-util: 62%
```

Jamal: kvcache_miss rate ~9.4% of accesses — not tiny, but not catastrophic either. Could be path selection: autotuner appears to pick KX-17 for seq>1024 on Ampere. Do we have the autotune decision log?

Anna: autotune snippet:
```
[autopick] seq_range=1025-4096 arch=ampere candidate=KX-17 score=0.87 reason="latency_profile v2"
[autopick] selected_kernel=KX-17 for route=/generate model=rw-v1.2
```

Ben: Compare baseline KX-12 (previous pick) numbers for same run and batch.

Priya: I ran KX-12 and KX-17 across batch sizes 1/2/4 and quant levels (fp16/int8). Quick table:`
```
arch=ampere seq=2048 runs=200
KX-12 fp16 batch=4 p50=3.30ms p99=8.1ms
KX-17 fp16 batch=4 p50=3.87ms p99=9.2ms  <-- current candidate
KX-17 int8  batch=4 p50=3.60ms p99=8.9ms
KX-12 int8  batch=4 p50=3.20ms p99=7.9ms
```

Priya: Notes: KX-17 seems to have slightly worse tail latency on long sequences, and int8 helps a bit but not enough to close p99 gap.

Jamal: Hypothesis: KX-17's kernel path does extra KV-cache population or different prefill behavior for long seqs which amplifies p99 under batching. Can we test with prefill enabled vs disabled? `--prefill-kv` flag exists in kbench.

Anna: Ran quick run with `--prefill-kv` enabled, same cmd: p50->3.50ms, p99->8.0ms. So prefill removes most of the tail gap. Snip:
```
KX-17 fp16 batch=4 prefill=true p50=3.50ms p99=8.0ms
```

Ben: That suggests the delta comes from on-the-fly KV population cost interacting with batching. Onwards: either avoid KX-17 for seq>1024 until we fix the prefill or gate candidates that show >5% p50 or >10% p99 regression.

Anna: Agreed. Current dedicated rollout used the autopick policy that permitted KX-17 broadly. We should patch autopick to require an instrumentation sweep that includes kvcache counters and `--prefill-kv` comparison for longseq arch=ampere.

deploy-bot: Created ticket RW-9872: "Autopick gating: require kvcache + prefill sweep for long-seq ampere candidates" assigned to @Jamal.

Jamal: I'll add a CI job: nightly-longseq-ampere-prefill that runs candidate permutations (batch 1/2/4, prefill on/off, quant levels) and fails the candidate if p50 delta>5% OR p99 delta>12% vs baseline. Will also emit `kvcache_hit/miss` time series to Datadog.

Priya: Also propose adding a microprobe that forces mid-sequence checkpoints in kbench to measure incremental KV population cost per token. Could help pinpoint where overhead spikes.

Ben: Action list: (1) revert autopick rollout for KX-17 on ampere longseq (Anna) (2) run Jamal's expanded CI sweep overnight (Jamal) (3) add microprobe check (Priya) (4) create follow-up perf engineering spike to optimize KX-17 prefill/pop behavior (Anna/Priya).

Anna: Reverted rollout in the console for the canary pool. Notified impacted teams. :eyes:

perf-bot: [CI] nightly-longseq-ampere-prefill scheduled, will post results in #eng-runtime when done.

Ben: Thanks everyone. If the CI reproduces with prefills showing large kv miss/drift then we should hotfix kernel runtime to change the population strategy (deferred vs batched prefill).

Anna: I'll add the repro commands + log pointers to RW-9872 and include links to the kbench runs: https://ci.redwood/artifacts/7732/kbench-KX-17-ampere-2048.log

Jamal: On it — will share initial sweep summary in the morning. :shipit:
